title: SPARC - Acute Surgery and Experimentation of the Gastrointestinal Tract and Vagus Nerve in Ferrets
author: Charles C Horn
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.6a7hahn
materials: Euthanize animal with intracardiac euthasol injection.

steps.title: Pre-operative Preparation
steps.instruction: Prepare the ferret for anesthesia and baseline measurements.

substeps.instruction: Remove food from the home cage 3 hours before anesthesia.
Measure body weight.

steps.title: Anesthesia and Initial Setup
steps.instruction: Induce anesthesia and establish vital sign monitoring.

substeps.instruction: Induce anesthesia using isoflurane in a chamber, then transition to a facemask (1 to 2%).
Place ferret supine on the table.
Connect EKG leads and place a rectal probe to monitor body temperature (maintain between 36 to 40°C).
Insert an endotracheal tube and connect to a pressure transducer (Small Animal Ventilator, CWe, SAR-830/AP) to monitor respiration rate.
Place a blood pressure catheter in the left femoral artery using a Direct Blood Pressure System (Kent Scientific, DBP1000).
Monitor heart rate and body temperature throughout the procedure using CED Power 1401 running Spike 2 version 7.15.

steps.title: Surgical Access and Instrumentation
steps.instruction: Perform necessary incisions to access the gastrointestinal tract and nerves.

substeps.instruction: Make a ~3 cm incision on the medial surface of the right leg.
Make a ~4 cm incision in the ventral neck and dissect the trachea.
Make an incision in the midline abdominal muscle to expose the organs.

Open the abdominal cavity using a 3-point retractor (Balfour pediatric retractor, George Tiemann) applied to the lateral edges of the abdominal incision and sternum, elevated by a vertical post attached to a surgical board.

steps.title: Gastric Catheter and Balloon Placement
steps.instruction: Insert gastric instrumentation and secure the incision.

substeps.instruction: Make a ~0.5 cm incision on the left lateral edge of the gastric fundus.
Insert a gastric catheter with the tip resting in the antrum and a 30 ml barostat balloon in parallel.
Place and tie a purse-string suture around the incision.
Tie an additional knot around the catheter, then tie the free ends of this knot and the purse-string suture together.
Apply surgical glue (Vetbond) to the incision area.
Place planar electrodes on the surface of the stomach and duodenum using 8-0 silk suture.
Suture a ground electrode lead to connective tissue on the greater curvature of the stomach.

If required for the experiment, place a cuff electrode on either the ventral or dorsal abdominal vagus nerve trunk (access the esophagus and vagi via caudal retraction of the stomach and retraction of the liver to the right using saline-moistened gauze).

steps.title: Baseline Recording and Impedance Testing
steps.instruction: Verify electrode function and record initial activity using the Grapevine Neural Interface Processor and Nano2 recording headstage (Ripple LLC).

substeps.instruction: Test and measure electrode impedances.
Record 20 minutes of baseline gastrointestinal myoelectric activity.

steps.title: Experimental Testing
steps.instruction: Perform specific tests to evaluate gastrointestinal responses.

substeps.instruction: For stomach distension: Fill the balloon using a syringe pump with 5 ml, 10 ml, or 20 ml saline at a rate of 10 ml/min; hold saline for 5 minutes before deflation. Record 5 minutes of baseline before and after each trial.
For nerve stimulation: Apply desired stimulation parameters (pulse width, current amplitude, frequency) to the abdominal vagus while recording. Record baseline data before and after trials.
For emetine infusion: Use a syringe pump to infuse 5 mg/kg emetine into the stomach and record for 1 hour.

steps.title: Procedure Completion
steps.instruction: Terminate the experiment and remove instrumentation.

substeps.instruction: Open the abdomen and remove electrodes, balloon, and catheter.
